title: Red brake warning light on
h1: Why is my red brake warning light on?
metaDesc: Red brake light on? Find out in a few questions if it's the parking brake, low brake fluid or a brake system fault, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: brake light on but parking brake off
parking brake light wont go off
is it safe to drive with brake light on
intro: The red BRAKE light (often the word BRAKE or an exclamation mark in a circle) is one of the most important lights on the dash. Sometimes it's just the parking brake, but it can also mean low brake fluid or a fault in the braking system. A few quick checks help narrow down which, but only an inspection can confirm it.
safety: If the brake pedal feels soft, sinks toward the floor, or the car is slow to stop, pull over safely and don't drive on.
If you see clear to brownish oily fluid near a wheel or under the car by the pedal area, don't drive it.
If you smell burning or see smoke from a wheel, stop and let it cool. A brake may be stuck on.

If smoke continues, you see flames or you suspect a fire, pull over safely and switch off the vehicle. Get everyone out, move at least 100 feet away and clear of traffic, and call 911. Stay away from the vehicle.

q_pedal.q: How do the brakes feel and how is the car stopping?
q_pedal.help: A healthy pedal feels firm and stops well above the floor. If the car is parked, start the engine and press the pedal firmly for about 10 seconds.

opts.a: Soft, spongy, or sinking toward the floor, or the car takes longer to stop
I'm not sure, or I haven't driven it since the light came on

q_parking.q: Is the parking brake fully released?
q_parking.help: The parking brake may be a hand lever, a small pedal by your left foot, or a button marked P or with a brake symbol. Push it all the way down or release it fully, then watch the light.

opts.a: It was partly on. I released it and the light went out
It's fully released and the light stays on
It's an electric parking brake button, and there's a fault message or the light is flashing

q_fluid.q: With the engine off, where is the brake fluid level in the reservoir?
q_fluid.help: The reservoir is a small see-through plastic tank, usually high on the driver's side near the back of the engine bay. The cap often says brake fluid or DOT 3/DOT 4, and the side has MIN and MAX marks.

opts.a: At or below the MIN mark
I can't find it or I'm not sure

q_leak.q: Do you see any sign of a leak?
q_leak.help: Brake fluid is clear to light brown and feels slick, a bit like light oil. Check the ground under each wheel, the inside of each tire, and under the car near the brake pedal.

opts.a: Yes, wet or oily spots near a wheel, on a tire, or under the car
No leak that I can see

q_abs_too.q: Is the amber ABS light on as well?

opts.a: Yes, the ABS light is on too
No, only the red brake light

result.title: The brakes may be losing pressure. This is a safety problem
result.now: Don't drive it. Have the car towed or have a mobile mechanic inspect the brakes where it is.
if: If you're on the road now, slow down gently, shift to a lower gear, and use the parking brake gradually if the pedal won't stop you. Pull over somewhere safe.
If you see fluid dripping, tell the tow or repair service so they bring the right parts.
result.why: A red brake light with a soft or sinking pedal usually means the hydraulic system can't build normal pressure. That often comes from a fluid leak or a master cylinder problem, and braking can get worse without warning.

causes.name: Brake fluid leak
causes.clues: Low fluid in the reservoir, or wet spots near a wheel or on the inside of a tire.

causes.name: Master cylinder problem
causes.clues: The pedal slowly sinks under steady pressure with no visible leak.

causes.name: Air in the brake lines
causes.clues: Recent brake work, and the pedal has felt spongy since.

result.title: Often this is a parking brake that isn't fully released
result.now: Release the parking brake all the way. Push a lever fully down, press a foot pedal to release it, or press the electric button with your foot on the brake. Then check that the light goes out.
if: If the red brake light stays on after full release, keep the vehicle parked. Arrange a brake inspection where it is or a tow.

If smoke continues, you see flames or you suspect a fire, pull over safely and switch off the vehicle. Get everyone out, move at least 100 feet away and clear of traffic, and call 911. Stay away from the vehicle.
If the pedal feels soft or sinks, the car is slow to stop or pulls to one side, or you smell burning from a wheel, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
result.why: The same red light shows when the parking brake is on, and a lever pulled up just one click can be enough to turn it on. It's the most common reason for this light and the simplest to fix.

causes.name: Parking brake partly applied
causes.clues: The light goes out when you fully release it.
causes.against: If it stays on with the brake fully released, look elsewhere.

causes.name: Parking brake switch sticking
causes.clues: The light flickers when you jiggle the lever or pedal.

causes.name: Low brake fluid
causes.clues: The light stays on with the parking brake off.

you: Release the parking brake fully and watch the light.
Jiggle the lever or pedal to see if the light flickers.

result.title: The electric parking brake may have a fault
result.now: Read the exact warning while parked and follow the owner’s manual. If the red brake-system light stays on, the pedal feels abnormal or the parking brake will not release, keep the vehicle parked and arrange assistance. If only the amber parking-brake fault is on and braking feels normal, contact the shop for the next step.
if: If the parking brake won't release, the car feels like it's dragging, or you smell burning from a rear wheel, don't drive it. Have it towed or call a mobile mechanic.
If the light came on right after a battery was replaced or jumped, restart the car once. Some systems need a moment to reset.
If the pedal feels soft or sinks, the car is slow to stop or pulls to one side, or you smell burning from a wheel, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
result.why: Cars with a parking brake button often flash the red brake light or show a message when the electric parking brake has a fault. The regular brakes work separately, but the parking brake may not hold the car or may not release properly, so have the whole brake system checked.

causes.name: Parking brake motor or caliper fault
causes.clues: A grinding or whirring sound at a rear wheel when you press the button.

causes.name: Low voltage after a battery problem
causes.clues: It started after a dead battery or jump start.

causes.name: Switch or wiring fault
causes.clues: The button doesn't respond at all.

you: Read the message on the dash and look it up in the owner's manual.
Note whether the parking brake applies and releases when you press the button.
shop: Parking brake motor and wiring test

result.title: Brake fluid may be leaking. The brakes could fail
result.now: Don't drive it, even after topping up the fluid. Have it towed or have a mobile mechanic come to you.
if: If you must move the car a few feet out of danger, do it very slowly and test the brakes first.
result.why: Low fluid plus a visible leak usually means the brake system is losing the fluid it needs to stop the car. Topping it up only hides the problem, and the leak can get worse suddenly.

causes.name: Leaking brake hose or line
causes.clues: Wet spots near a wheel or along the underside, often on older cars in salty areas.

causes.name: Leaking caliper or wheel cylinder
causes.clues: Fluid on the inside of one tire or wheel.

causes.name: Leaking master cylinder
causes.clues: Fluid under the car near the pedal area, or on the back of the engine bay.

result.title: Brake fluid is low with no visible leak. Get the brakes inspected before driving
result.now: Don't drive it until the brakes are inspected, even if the pedal feels normal. A mobile mechanic can come to you, or have it towed. Topping it up isn't a fix: low fluid can come from a leak you can't see or from badly worn pads.
if: If you have to move the car a few feet out of danger, do it very slowly and test the brakes first.
If the inspection finds worn pads and no leak, the shop will usually replace the pads and then set the fluid to the right level.
If you top it up, use only the fluid type printed on the cap, and still have the brakes inspected before driving.
result.why: Brake fluid doesn't get used up. The level falls slowly as brake pads wear, so a low level can mean the pads are thin. It can also mean fluid is escaping somewhere that's hard to see, such as inside a wheel or at the back of the engine bay. A website can't tell those apart, so it's safest to have it checked before the car is used.

causes.name: Worn brake pads
causes.clues: Squealing or grinding when braking, or no brake work in a long time.
causes.against: If the pads were replaced recently, a leak is more likely.

causes.name: Slow leak
causes.clues: The level keeps dropping after a top-up, or damp spots near a wheel.

causes.name: Master cylinder seals leaking
causes.clues: Dampness around the reservoir or behind the engine bay.

you: Look at the inside of each tire and under the car near the pedal area for wet, oily spots.
Look through the wheel spokes at the brake pad thickness if you can see it.

result.title: Brake and ABS lights together mean brake balance may be off
result.now: Don't drive it. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic to read the brake codes.
if: If both lights went out after a restart, still get the codes read soon. The fault is stored and may come back.
result.why: With fluid at a normal level, both lights on usually means the ABS system has a fault that also switches off electronic brake balance. That system keeps the rear wheels from locking in a hard stop. Without it, the car can skid or spin.

causes.name: Wheel speed sensor fault
causes.clues: Recent brake or wheel work, or a hard pothole hit.

causes.name: ABS module or pump fault
causes.clues: Both lights came on with no clear trigger.

causes.name: Low voltage after a battery problem
causes.clues: It started right after a dead battery or jump start.

you: Check whether both lights stay on after you turn the car off and restart it.
shop: ABS and brake system code scan

result.title: A persistent red brake warning needs inspection before driving
result.now: Stop safely and keep the vehicle parked if the red brake warning stays on with the parking brake released. Even if the pedal feels normal and fluid is in range, arrange a tow or inspection where it is parked.
if: If the pedal feels soft or sinks, the car is slow to stop or pulls to one side, or you smell burning from a wheel, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
If jiggling the parking brake makes the light flicker, the switch may be the cause. Mention that to the shop.
If the amber ABS light comes on as well, or the fluid level drops toward MIN, don't drive it until the brakes are checked.
result.why: With the parking brake off, fluid between the marks and a normal pedal, the light may be getting a false signal from a stuck fluid level float or a worn parking brake switch. A red brake light can also report other brake faults, so a shop should confirm the cause rather than assuming it's the switch.

causes.name: Parking brake switch sticking
causes.clues: The light flickers when you move the lever or pedal.

causes.name: Brake fluid level sensor sticking
causes.clues: Fluid is near the MIN mark, or the light flickers on turns or bumps.

causes.name: Brake system fault that needs a scan
causes.clues: On some cars, this light also reports other brake faults.

you: Note whether another warning or dashboard message appeared.

result.title: Treat a red brake light as serious until it's checked
result.now: Don't drive it until the brake fluid and brakes are checked. If you can't check them yourself, have it towed or ask a mobile mechanic to come to you.
if: If the red brake light remains on with the parking brake released, keep the vehicle parked and arrange an inspection or tow even when the fluid level and pedal feel normal.
result.why: With the parking brake off, the red light usually means low brake fluid or a brake system fault. Without knowing the fluid level, there's no safe way to rule out a problem that affects stopping.

causes.name: Low brake fluid
causes.clues: Worn pads, or wet spots near a wheel.

causes.name: Brake system or ABS fault
causes.clues: The ABS light is on too.

causes.name: Faulty switch or sensor
causes.clues: The brakes feel completely normal.

you: Make sure the parking brake is fully released.
Look under the car and inside each wheel for wet spots.
shop: Brake fluid level and leak check
